text: How many of those are whole-genome sequencing rather than RNA-Seq?

Abstract
This query asks, “How many of those are whole-genome sequencing rather than RNA-Seq?” The referent “those” is not specified in the current conversation, so no datasets or records have been retrieved yet. To answer reproducibly I planned to query federated dataset and sequencing-run resources that index assay types: NDE (federated datasets), ENA (raw run metadata), and NCBI SRA (run metadata). Because no prior set of records was provided, I performed no tool calls and therefore retrieved 0 datasets. I describe below the exact resources and the concrete query forms I will run once you confirm which collection “those” refers to (examples: the previous result set in this chat, all datasets for a named organism, a specific NDE/ENA/SRA query, or a list of accessions). I also list how counts will be computed (deduplicating by accession and grouping by library_strategy / measurementTechnique.name), and provide three ready-to-run query templates. Clarifying which “those” you mean will allow precise, tool-backed counts of whole-genome sequencing (WGS) versus RNA-Seq runs.

I. Introduction
Background. Distinguishing whole-genome sequencing (WGS) from RNA-Seq among a set of sequencing records is a common metadata-filtering task needed to select appropriate data for genomic versus transcriptomic analyses. Repositories that expose assay/library strategy fields include NDE (federated datasets), ENA (fastq/run metadata with library_strategy), and NCBI SRA (library strategy).
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. The specific set of records (“those”) to classify as WGS vs RNA-Seq is unspecified.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: given a defined input set of dataset/run identifiers or an explicit filter (organism, date range, search query), return the count and proportion that are WGS versus RNA-Seq. Hypothesis: in a well-specified query, assay-type counts can be obtained by querying NDE/ENA/SRA fields and deduplicating by run/accession.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. I will query one or more of these resources to count assay types:
- NDE federated dataset index (for dataset-level measurementTechnique.name and infectiousAgent/species context).
- ENA run search (for run-level library_strategy and total_matching).
- NCBI SRA search (for SRA run metadata and library strategy). I chose these because they directly expose assay/library strategy metadata needed to classify WGS vs RNA-Seq.
Materials. No database was queried yet. If you confirm the target set, I will use:
- nde_search_datasets (nde_search_datasets) for federated dataset counts,
- brc_ena_search (brc_ena_search) for ENA run-level counts,
- ncbi_sra_search (ncbi_sra_search) for SRA run-level verification.
Procedures. No tool calls were executed because the input set was not provided. To reproduce later, I will run one of these exact calls (examples):
1) nde_search_datasets with parameters { query: "<free-text or organism>", record_type: "Dataset", size: 100 } to list datasets and inspect measurementTechnique.name and repository fields.
2) brc_ena_search with parameters { organism: "Escherichia coli", library_strategy: "WGS", limit: 100 } to count WGS runs for E. coli (or replace "WGS" with "RNA-Seq").
3) ncbi_sra_search with parameters { organism: "Homo sapiens", strategy: "RNA-Seq", max_results: 200 } to list RNA-Seq runs.
Statistical Analysis. Counts will be exact integers from repository metadata fields. If both dataset- and run-level records are returned, I will deduplicate by run accession (ENA/SRA run accession) before computing proportions. Percentages will be computed as (count_type / total_count) * 100 with denominator = number of unique runs in the specified input set. Any filtering (e.g., latest_version_only) will be reported.

III. Results
Data Presentation. No records were retrieved because the set referred to by “those” was not specified; consequently no numeric table can be produced.
Findings. 0 records retrieved; therefore 0 WGS and 0 RNA-Seq counts computed.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. Without a defined input set or prior result to reference, the question cannot be answered. The methodology above will provide an exact answer once you specify which set to classify.
Context. The described approach maps directly to fields returned by the tools named (measurementTechnique.name in NDE, library_strategy in ENA/SRA). No external publications or dataset records were fetched.
Limitations. Repository metadata can be inconsistent: submitter-provided library_strategy fields sometimes use synonyms, mixed-case, or custom text; platform annotation may mislabel multiplexed experiments. The tools’ responses may be paged or truncated; when run I will report total_matching (ENA) or full counts and any warnings returned by the tool. Deduplication depends on consistent run accessions being present.
Conclusion & Future Directions. To proceed, please clarify which “those” you mean by choosing one of the options below or supplying identifiers:
- Option A: “the datasets you previously returned” — paste the earlier result list or accession(s).
- Option B: “All datasets for organism X in date range Y” — supply organism name and date range.
- Option C: “A federated search (free text)” — provide the search terms (I will run nde_search_datasets).
- Option D: “Run-level count on ENA or SRA” — specify organism and whether to prefer ENA or SRA.
Once you choose, I will run the appropriate tool(s) with exact parameters, deduplicate by run accession, and report a table with counts and percentages.
